title: Follow a recording through the pipeline
description: An introduction to asynchronous intake, enrichment and notification, and how workflows extend the baseline.

chapters.title: Media and events take different paths

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Imagine a fictional shop camera producing a motion recording. The video reaches Vault. How does Hub learn that there is something new to process?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Vault publishes an event to the message broker. The pipeline follows that event through small services with separate responsibilities. The media remains in storage while messages carry the information needed to move processing forward.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So this isn't one giant request waiting for every possible result?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Exactly. The broker connects the steps asynchronously. That makes independent workers possible, but it also means that storage, processing completion and the appearance of every result aren't one simultaneous event.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What happens before the interesting previews and labels arrive?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Monitoring validates the incoming activity and updates operational information such as usage and account limits. Sequencing organises recording metadata. These steps make the event useful to Hub before optional enrichment adds more detail.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That explains why a processing problem isn't always an inference problem.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Yes. If our shop recording never reaches the expected stage, check intake and routing first. A healthy model worker can't fix an event that never arrives at its queue.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Does one service generate thumbnails, timeline previews and every classification?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: The analyser coordinates separate workers. A thumbnail supplies a poster image; a sprite supports timeline scrubbing; classification adds detected-object information. Enabled services can work independently. Dominant colour is optional and its deployment setting also controls whether it is scheduled.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So a recording can be useful before every extra is present?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Right. Inspect the particular missing output rather than treating all enrichment as one opaque box. The diagram and individual sections show which worker owns which result.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What happens at the end of the baseline path?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Throttling limits event bursts before notification rules decide what to deliver through configured channels. A recording being stored doesn't mean every event must send a message.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And where do custom workflows fit?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: They provide configurable processing choices around cameras, timing and stages, and are the documented future direction. Treat this pipeline as the current static baseline, not a promise that every deployment runs every illustrated worker or that workflows have already replaced it.

editorialStyle.tone: A short, high-level introduction for a first-time listener. Explain why the topic matters, build one mental model, and suggest one next action. Sound like two colleagues, not a narrated manual.
editorialStyle.scope: Aim for four to five minutes and roughly 500-550 spoken words. Use one fictional example and four short chapters. Leave identifiers, form limits, configuration, migration mechanics, and troubleshooting checklists in the linked guide. Keep essential caveats as practical consequences.
editorialStyle.humour: Optional: one or two brief, relevant light moments are enough. Prefer a relatable analogy over a separate joke. Never pad the overview with banter.
editorialStyle.reactions: Use occasional short, natural responses such as 'Oh, that makes sense' or 'Wait, so...' followed by a real question. Avoid repetitive praise, canned agreement, and filler.
editorialStyle.laughter: Optional: at most one or two light reactions such as 'Ha, fair point.' Never insert [laughs], SSML, or repeated ha-ha strings. These are spoken reactions, not a guarantee of genuine laughter from the current speech engine.
editorialStyle.intonation: Write real questions with question marks, use contractions, alternate short and longer sentences, and make contrasts explicit. Let punctuation and sentence rhythm suggest curiosity, surprise, and emphasis. Avoid all-caps shouting, excessive exclamation marks, and artificial pause tags.
editorialStyle.guardrails: Keep technical claims source-backed. Never mock the listener, joke about real victims, minimize security or data-loss risks, or let humour replace an explanation. Personality is optional; accuracy and clarity are not.
